attack_mechanism: For computed control transfers, the ALU and register-file datapaths produce `reg_dest_val_in`, which becomes `pc_sw` when R0 is the destination or a CALL requests a PC write. Corrupting `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.alu_short` during target calculation changes one or more bits of the value presented to the software-PC input. `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.alu_short` contributes data or a selector to this computed target; the transfer is guarded in the RTL by `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.inst_alu`, `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.inst_bw`, `openMSP430.frontend_0.pc_sw_wr`. At the following PC write, execution is redirected to an unintended aligned or misaligned address. The affected transfer sequence is `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.alu_short -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.alu_out_nxt -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.reg_dest_val_in -> openMSP430.frontend_0.pc_nxt -> openMSP430.frontend_0.pc`.

With no software PC write and no interrupt-vector state active, `pc_nxt` falls through to `pc_incr = pc + {14'h0, fetch, 1'b0}`. Injecting a transient or stuck fault into `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.dst_inst_sext_sel` before `pc` is enabled can add the wrong increment or prevent the expected increment. `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.dst_inst_sext_sel` affects `fetch`, instruction length, or the instruction-state decision used by this sequential increment; the transfer is guarded in the RTL by `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.dbg_halt_st`, `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.dst_inst_sext_sel`, `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.inst_bw`, `openMSP430.frontend_0.pc_sw_wr`. The next instruction is skipped, repeated, or fetched from an unintended address. The affected transfer sequence is `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.dst_inst_sext_sel -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.op_dst -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.alu_out_nxt -> openMSP430.frontend_0.pc_nxt -> openMSP430.frontend_0.pc`.
